papers.title: Experiment-free exoskeleton assistance via learning in simulation
papers.authors_short: Luo S, Jiang M, Zhang S, ... Zhou X, Su H
papers.code_status: Pseudocode only: 4 files, no licence or releases, head 422a9c1 (2025-06-03); org has no newer repo (checked 2026-09-23). Nature Editor's Note dated 2026-07-27 flags data/code availability.
papers.api_title: Experiment-free exoskeleton assistance via learning in simulation
papers.core_idea: PPO jointly trains muscle, imitation and exoskeleton networks in a DART/MASS musculoskeletal model with bushing-coupled exoskeleton and domain randomisation. Deployed law: 128x64 MLP maps both thighs' IMU angle/velocity (current plus three 10-ms samples) to low-passed PD setpoints; walking −24.3% vs no-exo.
papers.what_to_take: Its policy sees ~40 ms of thigh angle/velocity, so fitted state-feedback laws (DOFC, k·ω) are the natural matched controls; copy its assist-on/assist-off/no-exo design and second-difference action-smoothness reward.
papers.left_untested: No same-device comparison with any simple controller; no training curves, seeds or complete reward constants; Editor's Note (27 Jul 2026) flags data/code availability; energy ratio disputed (Collins 5.5 vs Luo 2.4).
papers.feasibility_notes: Exact reproduction blocked (DART/MASS assets, weights absent); reimplement its observation/action contract in MyoAssist as a secondary learned baseline.

papers.title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance remains an unsolved problem
papers.authors_short: Collins SH, De Groote F, Gregg RD, Huang H, Lenzi T, Sartori M, Sawicki GS, Si J, Slade P, Young AJ
papers.code_status: Analysis code stated as Supplementary Data 1 and replication data as Source Data; not downloaded
papers.api_title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance remains an unsolved problem
papers.core_idea: Plausibility audit plus replication. Luo's torque times open-dataset hip velocity implies 5.5 J metabolic saved per J positive exo work (theoretical ceiling ≈4; best prior hip ≈2.3). Replaying Luo's mean torque profile (0/5/10/15% phase shifts) on a 4.8-kg hip exoskeleton, n=10: no significant reduction.
papers.what_to_take: Report positive exo power and energy ratio beside every saving, simulated or measured; replaying a learned policy's mean torque profile with phase-shift sweeps is a cheap, pointed matched baseline.
papers.left_untested: Zero-torque cost was modelled (0.045 W/kg per kg), not measured; the learned feedback policy was unavailable, and the rig was not first validated with an established controller such as DOFC.
papers.feasibility_notes: Energy-ratio check is nearly free in simulation: integrate positive exo power and compare with the simulated metabolic change.

papers.title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance is not an unsolved problem
papers.authors_short: Luo S, Jiang M, Zhang S, ... Zhou X, Su H
papers.code_status: Claims release of executable code, raw data and simulation files; no destination located (author GitHub org unchanged since 2025-06-03, Zenodo search empty, 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Experiment-free learning of exoskeleton assistance is not an unsolved problem
papers.core_idea: Rebuttal: energy ratio 4 is average muscle efficiency, not a ceiling; recomputed walking ratio ≈2.4 (24.9 W), ≈3.4 after an 18% timing correction; replication invalid: heel-strike-referenced (Luo's phase 0 = torque peak), averaged open-loop profile, heavier device with unmeasured mass penalty.
papers.what_to_take: Define phase zero explicitly, validate any rig with a known controller (they suggest DOFC), and measure the zero-torque mass penalty—these are the confounds a SMAT-versus-baseline comparison must pre-register.
papers.left_untested: Claimed code/data release not located; 'Zhou 2025 ≈20% running' is absent from the abstract of the only cited Zhou paper (ROBIO 2025: walking, n=3, 12.5-15.7%); Barati's quoted energy ratios above 4 unchecked.
papers.feasibility_notes: Use its confound list (timing reference, device mass, averaged versus individual profiles) as pre-registration items.

papers.title: Delayed Output Feedback Control for Gait Assistance With a Robotic Hip Exoskeleton
papers.authors_short: Lim B, Lee J, Jang J, Kim K, Park YJ, Seo K, Shim Y
papers.code_status: No author code; third-party DOFC implementation in Exo-Plore src/core/Device.cpp (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
papers.api_title: Delayed Output Feedback Control for Gait Assistance With a Robotic Hip Exoskeleton
papers.core_idea: Delayed output feedback control: y(t)=sin θR(t)−sin θL(t) from low-pass-filtered hip angles; τR(t)=−κ·y(t−Δt), τL(t)=+κ·y(t−Δt) (form and signs as coded in Exo-Plore). Two parameters, no phase or terrain estimator; stability analysed on a leg-swing model; treadmill metabolic validation.
papers.what_to_take: Primary matched baseline: phase-free, deployable sensors only, two parameters. Tune (κ, Δt) with the same torque cap, RMS budget and simulator budget as SMAT; Exo-Plore's human-matched setting is κ=8 Nm, Δt=0.25 s.
papers.left_untested: Abstract reports no effect size (Luo 2026 cites ≈19.8-21% at 10.9 Nm peak); no running or sprint tests in the abstract; never compared with a simulation-trained policy on the same device.
papers.feasibility_notes: Trivial in MyoAssist: filtered-angle ring buffer plus a 2-D (κ, Δt) sweep; Exo-Plore bounds κ∈[0,21] Nm, Δt∈[0,0.5] s.

papers.title: Task-agnostic exoskeleton control via biological joint moment estimation
papers.authors_short: Molinaro DD, Scherpereel KL, Schonhaut EB, Evangelopoulos G, Shepherd MK, Young AJ
papers.code_status: Code Ocean capsule to deploy/test trained estimators and dataset doi:10.35090/gatech/75759, both linked in the paper; not executed
papers.api_title: Task-agnostic exoskeleton control via biological joint moment estimation
papers.core_idea: Moment-proportional control: a TCN estimates hip and knee biological moments from onboard exoskeleton sensors; command = 20% (hip) or 15% (knee) of the estimate, delayed 100 ms (hip) or 50 ms (knee), low-pass filtered. Energetics fell 5.3-19.7% vs zero-torque across ten activities.
papers.what_to_take: In simulation the true hip moment is free, so τ=0.2·M_hip(t−0.1 s), low-passed and capped, is a strong oracle baseline; add estimator-level noise for a deployable variant.
papers.left_untested: Beat an idealised classifier/spline/impedance baseline, but no comparison with phase-free kinematic laws (DOFC, damping) or simulation-trained policies; Collins et al. compute its level-walking energy ratio at only 0.8.
papers.feasibility_notes: Dataset and deployment code released; oracle moments come free from MuJoCo muscle forces, so this baseline costs one extra rollout config.

papers.title: End-to-End Policy Learning for Hip Exoskeleton via Reinforcement Learning and Reflex-Based Musculoskeletal Simulation
papers.authors_short: Barati H, Kim S, Nguyen X, Lee J, Park YJ
papers.code_status: No public code found (GitHub search 2026-09-23); paywalled, read at abstract level
papers.api_title: End-to-End Policy Learning for Hip Exoskeleton via Reinforcement Learning and Reflex-Based Musculoskeletal Simulation
papers.core_idea: Hip-torque policy trained by LSTM-PPO (vs an MLP-PPO baseline) against a reflex-driven planar musculoskeletal walker with domain randomisation and sensor-noise injection, deployed directly on a lightweight hip exoskeleton; n=8 treadmill: net metabolic −15.2% (LSTM) and −11.0% (MLP) vs unassisted walking.
papers.what_to_take: A reflex-model human plus randomisation sufficed for transfer; policy memory shifted benefit by ~4 points, so comparisons must match observation history and architecture, not only torque budget.
papers.left_untested: No simple-controller or zero-torque-matched comparison reported in the abstract; 'unassisted' comparator undefined there; Luo 2026 reports 4/8 subjects above energy ratio 4, which Collins' criterion would flag.
papers.feasibility_notes: Planar reflex walker is cheap on a 64-core CPU; full text paywalled and no public code, so reconstruct from the paper.

papers.title: Adaptive Negative Damping Control for User-Dependent Multi-Terrain Walking Assistance With a Hip Exoskeleton
papers.authors_short: Ramella G, Ijspeert A, Bouri M
papers.api_title: Adaptive Negative Damping Control for User-Dependent Multi-Terrain Walking Assistance With a Hip Exoskeleton
papers.core_idea: Virtual negative damping: Γ = β·R·q̇, R=[1 −1; 0 1] acting on stance and swing hip velocities (4-Hz filtered; stance leg = extending leg by velocity sign), β∈[1.0, 2.5] N·m·s/rad, adapted online by Bayesian optimisation of hip ROM minus jerk.
papers.what_to_take: Human anchor for the velocity-proportional baseline: fixed β=2.3 cut metabolic cost 7.2% vs free walking (n=5, 1.1 m/s, 4.4-kg eWalk) with <2% negative power; the programme's k·ω law is a single-joint, low-passed variant.
papers.left_untested: Five participants, one treadmill speed, no zero-torque or phase-profile comparator; the optimiser's ROM-minus-jerk objective is not energetic; running-speed stability untested.
papers.feasibility_notes: Minutes to implement in MyoAssist; sweep β at equal RMS torque against SMAT.

papers.title: Versatile Exoskeleton Control Supports Elderly Joint Energetics During Hip-Intensive Tasks
papers.authors_short: Zhang J, Divekar NV, Krishnan C, Gregg RD
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering (early access, record created 2026-09-10); arXiv v2 2026-08-13
papers.api_title: Versatile Exoskeleton Control Supports Elderly Joint Energetics During Hip-Intensive Tasks
papers.core_idea: Velocity-modulated virtual springs: unidirectional extension and flexion torsion springs on hip angle, each scaled by a sigmoid of hip angular velocity, plus task-context attenuation for descent and a torso-gated sit-to-stand spring; fixed parameters across tasks, 250 Hz, 4.6-kg device.
papers.what_to_take: A second velocity-based law with 2026 human data: velocity gating aligns torque with positive hip power (power-profile cosine similarity 0.89); hip biological positive work fell 24.7% in eight older adults.
papers.left_untested: No metabolic or running data—biological work is a mechanical endpoint; parameters were tuned by optimisation plus one young user's feedback before testing older adults.
papers.feasibility_notes: Sigmoid-gated spring is three lines of code; exact coefficients are in equation images—extract from the PDF before implementing.

papers.title: Effects of Assistance Delay on Joint Mechanics and Energetics in Biological Torque Control of a Hip Exoskeleton
papers.authors_short: An J, Lee R, Peng J, Halilaj E, Kang I
papers.api_title: Effects of Assistance Delay on Joint Mechanics and Energetics in Biological Torque Control of a Hip Exoskeleton
papers.core_idea: Biological torque control τ(t)=filter(0.2·M̂hip(t−d)), capped 18 Nm, M̂ from a single-thigh-IMU TCN (950-ms window); delays 40-320 ms vs zero-torque, n=8, level/ramp walking. Delay changed joint-work unloading but not net metabolic rate (−5.24% overall; +1.23% on descent).
papers.what_to_take: Mechanical proxies and metabolic outcome diverged across delays, so simulated muscle-activation or joint-work savings (SMAT's metric) must not be read as metabolic; sweep delay for the moment baseline.
papers.left_untested: Scale fixed at 0.2; no kinematic-law or learned-policy comparator; eight participants, level and ramp walking only; preprint, not yet peer reviewed.
papers.feasibility_notes: Same oracle-moment pipeline as Molinaro; a five-level delay sweep is cheap in simulation.

papers.title: Design and Validation of a Modified Delayed Output Feedback Controller for Hip Exoskeleton Assistance
papers.authors_short: Yoon S, Lee D, Lee HJ, Koo S
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering 34:1921-1931 (record created 2026-04-08)
papers.code_status: none found; article CC BY 4.0 but IEEE PDF blocked here, read at abstract level
papers.api_title: Design and Validation of a Modified Delayed Output Feedback Controller for Hip Exoskeleton Assistance
papers.core_idea: Modified DOFC adds harmonic components to delayed, amplified hip-angle feedback, still tuned by two parameters; parameters optimised in forward-dynamics gait simulation driven by an RL neural controller, then tested on people: metabolic reduction comparable to DOFC with 8.8% less mechanical power.
papers.what_to_take: Closest precedent for 'optimise a simple law in an RL-driven gait simulation, then transfer'; also check closed-loop stability of every baseline (they report stability up to 45 W via short-term Lyapunov exponents).
papers.left_untested: Harmonic form, participant count and effect sizes not seen (abstract only); walking only; no comparison against a learned policy or velocity-based law.
papers.feasibility_notes: Open access (CC BY 4.0); fetch the PDF from IEEE or PubMed (PMID 41950129) to get the harmonic formula.

papers.title: Optimized Mappings From Biological Hip Moment Estimates to Exoskeleton Torque Can Personalize Assistance Across Users and Generalize Across Tasks
papers.authors_short: Powell JC, Schonhaut EB, Molinaro DD, Young AJ
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics 8(3):1218-1229 (Aug 2026); preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.08.29.671780
papers.api_title: Optimized Mappings From Biological Hip Moment Estimates to Exoskeleton Torque Can Personalize Assistance Across Users and Generalize Across Tasks
papers.core_idea: Mid-level mapping of a TCN hip-moment estimate: scale α (held at 20% of peak), delay d (65-240 ms) and power-law shape λ (0.5-1.6), clipped at 18 Nm; human-in-the-loop Bayesian optimisation of (d, λ) on metabolic cost, n=9, three walking conditions.
papers.what_to_take: Same law, different tuning: personalised 18.3% vs task-agnostic 8.4% saving (both vs no-exo). Give every baseline SMAT's parameter-search budget, or tuning effort masquerades as controller class.
papers.left_untested: Walking only (1.1, 1.5 m/s, 5° incline); scale fixed; no kinematic-law or learned-policy comparator; preference and metabolic landscapes correlated at r=0.69.
papers.feasibility_notes: Two-parameter sweep over oracle or noisy simulated hip moments; cheap.

papers.title: Evaluation of controllers for augmentative hip exoskeletons and their effects on metabolic cost of walking: explicit versus implicit synchronization
papers.authors_short: Manzoori AR, Malatesta D, Primavesi J, Ijspeert A, Bouri M
papers.api_title: Evaluation of controllers for augmentative hip exoskeletons and their effects on metabolic cost of walking: explicit versus implicit synchronization
papers.core_idea: Same device, two simple laws, 23 naive walkers at 4 km/h: Simple Reflex Controller (torque from relative foot loading: stance extension, swing flexion; implicit synchronisation) vs hip-phase-based predefined torque bursts (explicit). Metabolic −18.0% vs −11.6% relative to passive device.
papers.what_to_take: Only the reflex law beat no-exo (−8.8%): report no-device, passive/zero-torque and assisted arms; include one continuous state-driven law and one phase profile in the matched set.
papers.left_untested: Torque magnitude and delivered power were not matched between controllers (SRC gave more power); single speed; no learned controller.
papers.feasibility_notes: Foot-contact forces are free MuJoCo sensor readings; both laws are simple to replicate.

papers.title: Learning Hip Exoskeleton Control Policy via Predictive Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation
papers.authors_short: Park I, Song C, Kang I
papers.code_status: Precursor only: 89 files (SCONE models, synergy matrix, SAC scripts), no licence, releases, weights or TCN/distillation code; head e5c55db 2025-12-19, pushed 2026-06-26 (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Learning Hip Exoskeleton Control Policy via Predictive Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation
papers.core_idea: SAC teacher jointly drives a 90-muscle SCONE/Hyfydy model (synergy action prior) and bilateral hip torque over speeds and slopes; a TCN student maps 0.95 s of one thigh gyro to hip torque; hardware torque waveforms matched simulation (r=0.82, RMSE 0.03 Nm/kg, n=5).
papers.what_to_take: Transfer-check recipe: compare sim and real sensor channels, distil to deployable inputs, report student-teacher error and per-condition waveform agreement; borrow for SMAT's reconstruction.
papers.left_untested: No metabolic or muscle outcome on hardware; logged torque may be command rather than delivered; downhill agreement weak (r=0.66); no simple-controller baseline.
papers.feasibility_notes: Walk-RL precursor needs SCONE with the Hyfydy engine; distillation code, student data and weights absent.

papers.title: Exo-Plore: Exploring Exoskeleton Control Space through Human-aligned Simulation
papers.authors_short: Leem G, Lee J, Lee J, Song S, Won J
papers.code_status: Public, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: 407-entry tree (DART C++ environment, RL gait generator, surrogate, GEMS hip-device model, figure scripts); no trained checkpoints; head e3de238 2026-08-04 (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Exo-Plore: Exploring Exoskeleton Control Space through Human-aligned Simulation
papers.core_idea: Deep-RL musculoskeletal gait generator with metabolic plus human-exoskeleton-interaction (resistance-minimisation) reward, and a surrogate network, optimise DOFC τ=κ·[sin θr − sin θl](t−Δt) over κ∈[0,21] Nm, Δt∈[0,0.5] s; reproduces human assisted-gait trends; optimal delay falls with speed.

papers.title: Sensorless model-based tension control for a cable-driven exosuit
papers.authors_short: Bardi E, Esser A, Wolf P, Gandolla M, Ambrosini E, Pedrocchi A, Riener R
papers.code_status: none public; data and analysis scripts on request (per KB reading)
papers.api_title: Sensorless model-based tension control for a cable-driven exosuit
papers.core_idea: Force-sensor-free cable tension control: an inverse Bowden-friction model maps desired tension to motor torque using separate affine fits for raising and lowering, blended by a sigmoid of joint velocity (IMU); load cell used only for identification and evaluation.
papers.what_to_take: Bench baseline for Phase-2 torque delivery: identify direction-dependent friction, run feedforward compensation, quantify reversal errors—before crediting any high-level policy with an outcome.
papers.left_untested: Upper-limb gravity support only (n=17); torque RMSE 0.71 Nm (18%) at 50% support; no gait, sprint-rate reversals or bandwidth; printed sigmoid sign inconsistent (KB reading).
papers.feasibility_notes: Needs a load cell only for calibration; refit coefficients for each spool, sheath and routing.

papers.title: Finite-Time Robust Control for Bowden Cable-Driven Exoskeletons With Time-Varying Cable Configurations
papers.authors_short: Wang Z, Zhou Z, Mai J, Wang Q
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology 34(5):2901-2908 (Sep 2026)
papers.code_status: none found; read at abstract level
papers.api_title: Finite-Time Robust Control for Bowden Cable-Driven Exoskeletons With Time-Varying Cable Configurations
papers.core_idea: Nonsingular terminal sliding-mode tracking controller for multi-DOF Bowden-cable exoskeletons whose cable configuration changes with wearer motion; no accurate model parameters needed, finite-time convergence via Lyapunov analysis; validated in simulation and experiments on a Bowden-cable hip exoskeleton.
papers.what_to_take: Sprint hip excursions change cable routing quickly; test transmission tracking under time-varying configuration on the bench, separately from the assistance policy.
papers.left_untested: Tracking-only evaluation (abstract); no human energetic or performance outcome; sprint-rate reversals and slack not shown.
papers.feasibility_notes: Hardware-stage reference; for simulation only its transmission limits matter.

cluster_lessons: Matched baselines with human evidence already exist as two-parameter, phase-free laws: DOFC τ=κ[sin θR−sin θL](t−Δt) (Lim 2019; coded in Exo-Plore), negative damping Γ=βRq̇ (Ramella 2025), velocity-gated springs (Zhang 2026) and moment-proportional τ=α·M(t−d) (Molinaro 2024, Powell 2026, An 2026).

Deployed sim-trained policies see short proprioceptive windows (Luo: ~40 ms of thigh angle/velocity; Park: one thigh gyro), so they are functionally close to those laws. Fit the laws to the learned policy's torque and test whether the residual carries any benefit.

Comparator arms decide headlines: Manzoori's reflex law was −18% vs passive but −8.8% vs no-device; Collins modelled rather than measured the device-mass cost. Run no-device, zero-torque (mass-matched) and assisted arms for SMAT and every baseline.

Tuning budget is a confound as large as controller class: Powell's single law gave 18.3% personalised vs 8.4% task-agnostic. Give each baseline the same number of simulated evaluations as SMAT's policy search.

Report positive device power and the energy ratio with every saving. The Collins–Luo dispute turns on 5.5 vs 2.4 J saved per J; Collins puts the best prior hip value at ≈2.3. A simulated saving implying more than 4 should be treated as a modelling bug until explained.

Timing reference is a hidden parameter: Collins swept 0–15% shifts from heel strike, Luo defines phase 0 at peak torque, and An 2026 found delay changed joint work but not metabolic rate. Sweep delay or phase for every baseline and pre-register the phase definition.

Mechanical proxies are not metabolic outcomes (An 2026; Zhang 2026 reports work only; Park reports waveforms only). SMAT's simulated muscle-activation saving needs an explicit energetics model before it is compared with human metabolic results.

Transfer evidence is partial everywhere: Park shows waveform transfer without efficacy, Barati shows efficacy without simple baselines, and no complete code exists for Luo, Park or Barati. For cable exosuits, validate tension delivery on the bench (Bardi, Wang) before judging any high-level policy.
occupied_claims: Training a hip-exoskeleton policy entirely in musculoskeletal simulation and transferring it to hardware with a metabolic benefit (Luo 2024, contested; Barati 2026; SMAT 2026).
Distilling a privileged simulation teacher into a single-IMU student for hip assistance, validated by torque-waveform agreement (Park 2026).
Optimising DOFC-family parameters in RL or musculoskeletal gait simulation, including a human-trend validation and a sim-to-human transfer (Exo-Plore 2026; Yoon 2026).
Velocity-proportional (negative damping) or velocity-gated hip assistance lowering metabolic cost or biological work (Ramella 2025; Zhang 2026).
Scale/delay/shape mappings of estimated hip moment, including personalisation and delay sweeps against zero-torque (Molinaro 2024; Powell 2026; An 2026).
Energy-ratio plausibility audits of sim-to-real claims and fixed mean-profile replay replications (Collins 2026; rebutted by Luo 2026).
Head-to-head comparison of implicit (state-driven) and explicit (phase-based) hip controllers on one device with passive and no-device arms (Manzoori 2024).
Force-sensor-free model-based tension control for cable exosuits (Bardi 2024) and robust Bowden hip-exoskeleton tracking under time-varying cable configuration (Wang 2026).
open_gaps: No study found compares a simulation-trained hip policy with DOFC, velocity-proportional and phase-profile controllers at matched peak/RMS torque, positive power and tuning budget, either in simulation or on one device.
No energy-ratio (metabolic saving per joule of positive device work) check is reported for SMAT or any other simulation-trained hip policy's simulated benefit.
No fitted-law distillation test found: how much of a learned hip policy's torque, and of its benefit, a two-parameter DOFC or k·ω law reproduces.
No simulation-trained hip controller has been evaluated for sprinting or maximal running; the fastest learned-in-simulation hardware result found is Luo's 2 m/s running (13.1%), itself disputed.
No simulation-trained high-level policy transferred to a cable-driven hip exosuit with human outcomes was found; cable work covers low-level tension or tracking (Bardi 2024, Wang 2026).
Only DOFC has a simulated-versus-human trend validation (Exo-Plore); velocity-proportional and moment-proportional laws have none, so simulated baseline benefits are unvalidated.
Luo 2026's claimed code and data release could not be located on 2026-09-23, so the learning-in-simulation dispute still cannot be adjudicated by re-running the original pipeline.
